title: My phone has become slow
intro: A slow phone almost always comes from three things: full storage, too many apps running in the background, or an outdated system.

steps.d: Turn the phone off completely, wait 10 seconds, then turn it on again. This clears the memory and fixes many slowdowns.
Go to Settings → Storage. If less than 10% is free, the phone slows down. Delete videos, duplicates and large WhatsApp files (WhatsApp Settings → Storage and data).

steps.t: Close and uninstall what you do not need
steps.d: In Settings → Apps, see which ones use the most. Uninstall the ones you no longer use. Avoid having several "cleaner" apps: they often slow the phone down more than they help.

steps.t: Update the system and the apps
steps.d: Settings → System update, then Play Store → Manage apps & device. Do it on Wi-Fi so you do not use up your data plan.
In Developer options, set the animation scales to 0.5x or turn them off. The phone feels much faster, especially on an entry-level model.
First back up your photos and contacts (Google Photos, Google account), then go to Settings → Reset options. This erases everything: do it only if nothing else worked.

warn: If the phone gets very hot, drains very fast and is slow all at once, the battery may be worn out. Ask a technician to check it.

title: My phone does not charge or charges very slowly
intro: Before blaming the battery, check the cable, the charger and the port. These are the most common causes, especially when the power supply is unstable.

steps.t: Try another socket and another cable
steps.d: Cables wear out quickly. Try an original cable and charger, or ones from another phone of the same brand.
Turn off the phone and gently remove dust with a wooden toothpick or a dry toothbrush. Never use a metal object or any liquid.
A small software bug can stop charging. Sometimes a restart is enough.
Very cheap chargers deliver little power and can damage the battery. Choose a charger with the right power (shown on your original charger).

steps.t: Charge it while it is off
steps.d: If it charges when off but not when on, an app that uses a lot of power is the cause (or the battery is worn).

warn: Swollen battery, strong heat or a burning smell: stop charging, keep it away from anything that can burn, and have it replaced. Never puncture a battery.

title: Wi-Fi connected but no Internet
intro: If Wi-Fi says "connected" but there is no Internet, the problem is either on your device, on the router, or with the Internet provider. You need to find out which.

steps.d: If another phone or PC has Internet on the same Wi-Fi, the problem is your device. If none of them has Internet, it comes from the router or the provider.
In the Wi-Fi settings, tap "Forget network", then reconnect with the password.
Unplug it for 30 seconds, plug it back in, and wait 2 to 3 minutes for all the lights to settle.
An "Internet" or "WAN" light that is off, red or orange often means a line or data plan problem: call your provider or check that your data plan is not used up.
In the advanced Wi-Fi settings, set the DNS to 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4 (Google). This fixes cases where the connection exists but websites do not open.
A weak signal can show "connected" but let very little data through. Test at 2 meters from the router.

warn: If only some websites do not open, also try on mobile data: this tells you whether the block comes from the network or from the site.

title: My PC does not start
intro: First, observe what happens: nothing at all, a light, a black screen, an error message? Each case has a different lead.

steps.d: Socket, power strip, charger cable: try another socket. On a laptop, remove the battery if possible, hold the power button for 15 seconds, then plug in only the charger and turn it on again.
The charger or the power board may be faulty. Try a compatible charger. On a desktop PC, check the switch at the back of the case.

steps.t: It turns on but the screen is black
steps.d: On a desktop PC, connect another screen. Reseating the RAM module (with the PC off and unplugged) often fixes the problem: remove it and put it back firmly in place.

steps.t: Message "No bootable device" or "Operating system not found"
steps.d: The disk is no longer detected or the system is damaged. Enter the BIOS (press F2, F10, Delete or Esc at startup) and check whether the disk appears.
Start in Safe Mode (Windows: hold Shift while clicking Restart, then Troubleshoot). Uninstall the latest update or the last program you installed.
If the disk is detected, connect it to another PC (USB enclosure) to copy your files before reinstalling anything.

warn: If the hard drive makes repeated clicking noises, stop turning it on and ask a technician to recover the data.

title: My PC has become very slow
intro: A slow PC is often caused by too many programs at startup, an almost full disk, or a virus.

steps.d: Ctrl + Shift + Esc opens Task Manager. Sort by Memory and by Disk: a program that takes everything is your culprit.
In Task Manager, open the Startup tab and disable the useless programs (software updaters, launchers, etc.).
An almost full disk slows down Windows. Aim for at least 15% free space. Use "Disk Cleanup" and empty the Recycle Bin.
Use Microsoft Defender (already in Windows) for a full scan. Avoid installing several antivirus programs together.
If your PC still has a classic hard drive, switching to an SSD is the best upgrade possible, often more effective than buying a new computer.
With 4 GB or less, Windows and a browser with several tabs are enough to freeze everything. Going to 8 GB changes everything.

warn: Be careful with pirated software and unknown USB drives: they are the main sources of viruses on PCs.

title: My storage is full
intro: Almost always, it is photos, videos and files received on WhatsApp that fill the memory.

steps.t: Find out what takes up space
steps.d: Settings → Storage. Look at the breakdown: Images, Videos, Apps, Other.
WhatsApp → Settings → Storage and data → Manage storage. You will see the largest files and the ones forwarded many times: delete them.
Send photos and videos to Google Photos (or to a PC or a USB drive), check that they are there, then free up space on the phone.
Settings → Apps → choose a heavy app → Storage → Clear cache. Clearing the cache does not delete your data.
Heavy games and forgotten apps take up hundreds of MB.
If your phone accepts a microSD card, move your photos and videos there.

warn: Never delete a system folder if you do not know what it is for. When in doubt, do not touch it.

title: My account was hacked (Facebook, WhatsApp...)
intro: Act fast and in order: take back control, cut the hacker's access, then warn your contacts.

steps.t: Try to log in again and change your password
steps.d: Use "Forgot password" with your number or your email. Choose a long, unique password that you have never used anywhere else.
Facebook: Settings → Security → Where you're logged in. WhatsApp: Linked devices. Log out of everything you do not recognize.
This adds an extra code when you log in. On WhatsApp, turn on "Two-step verification" and choose a PIN that nobody knows.

steps.t: Never share a code received by SMS
steps.d: Most WhatsApp hacks happen by asking you for a "6-digit code sent by mistake". This code must never be shared, even with a friend.
Tell your friends and family not to answer money requests sent from your account. Hackers use it to scam your friends.

steps.t: If you can no longer log in
steps.d: Use the recovery form of the service concerned (Facebook: "My account is hacked", WhatsApp: write to their support from the app).

warn: Never pay anyone who claims to recover your account for money: it is almost always a second scam.

title: My Internet data plan runs out too fast
intro: A data plan that disappears is almost always explained by automatic updates, videos and apps running in the background.

steps.d: Settings → Network & internet → Data usage. You will see which app ate your data plan.

steps.t: Block automatic updates on mobile data
steps.d: Play Store → Settings → Network preferences → choose "Over Wi-Fi only" for updates and downloads.
On Facebook, TikTok, YouTube and WhatsApp, turn off video autoplay and lower the quality ("data saver").
Android: Settings → Data usage → Data Saver. It stops background apps from using the Internet.
In the same settings, set a threshold that warns you before you have used everything.
Download large files, apps and updates whenever you have access to Wi-Fi.

warn: Be careful with apps that promise to "boost" or "save" data: many are useless, and some collect your information.
